idea: A ratio a:b means the amounts are ak and bk for some k. When something is added to only one part, the other part stays fixed; write the new ratio as an equation in k.
trap: Treating “parts” as actual amounts, or adding to both parts when only one changes.
desmos: The equation in k is quick to solve once it is written down. Writing it is the skill.

items.stem: The ratio of boys to girls in a club is 3:5. There are 24 members in all. How many more girls than boys are in the club?
items.explain: The members are 3k boys and 5k girls, so 8k=24 and k=3. There are 15−9=6 more girls.

items.stem: A paint mixture is 1 part blue to 4 parts white. How many liters of blue paint must be added to 40 liters of this mixture to make a mixture that is half blue and half white?
items.explain: The 40 liters contain 51​(40)=8 liters of blue and 32 liters of white. Only blue is added, so blue must rise to 32: add 24 liters.
